source: Max Müller, Chips from a German Workshop I, as quoted/characterized by Garbe 1892
proof_problem: What similarities can establish Sāṃkhya/Buddhism relation?
inference_rule: Generic resemblance is insufficient; sufficiently definite similarities would be historically valuable
scope_limit: Garbe reports Müller as not finding such definite similarities
directionality: Could help decide Buddha→Kapila vs Kapila→Buddha

source: Aniruddha's Commentary ... Introduction on the Age and Origin of the Sāṃkhya System
proof_problem: How to prove dependence rather than mere resemblance?
diagnostic_evidence: details; external peculiarities involuntarily retained in expression; numerical/formal habits
inference_rule: Compare extant Sāṃkhya documents with early Buddhist records; rank details above generic agreement; infer connection before direction
scope_limit: Reject indefinitely pliable hypothetical lost proto-Sāṃkhya; common Indian traits or imperfect parallels do not suffice
directionality: Explicitly asks borrower/direction after diagnostic connection

proof_problem: Can early Buddhist evidence establish pre-Buddhist Sāṃkhya?
diagnostic_evidence: series of correspondences; Brahmajāla positions recognizable as Sāṃkhya doctrines
inference_rule: Uses correspondences plus textual witnesses to argue Sāṃkhya older than Buddha and a principal source
scope_limit: Concedes Brahmajāla's 62 schools cannot all be historical schools; catalogue systematizes theoretically possible opinions

proof_problem: When does formal resemblance reveal adopted material inside a system?
diagnostic_evidence: near-uniform terminology, definitions, detailed treatment, examples in inference theory
inference_rule: High-density formal agreement across schools is explained by adoption of Vaiśeṣika–Nyāya logic; same detailed apparatus in Sāṃkhya = fremdes Element
scope_limit: Alien material matters only insofar as it bears on method of Sāṃkhya system

proof_problem: How can formal agreement identify historical layering?
diagnostic_evidence: copies Garbe terminology/definitions/examples and alien-element inference
inference_rule: Directly absorbs Garbe 1894 diagnostic rule before listing pramāṇas
scope_limit: At this locus largely source uptake; not yet independent Lovejoy rule

proof_problem: What does an early Buddhist passage prove about Sāṃkhya?
diagnostic_evidence: presence/absence of technical term Prakṛti; doctrinal contradictions; separateness of Self and World; stronger Majjhima parallel
inference_rule: A passage may identify a genuinely Sāṃkhyan doctrine without proving the later Sāṃkhya system existed as a whole
scope_limit: Explicitly separates doctrine/diagnostic element from whole-system existence
directionality: Does not infer system-level genealogy from the weaker passage

proof_problem: How does the unit of historical inference change?
inference_rule: Lovejoy directly inherits one Garbean diagnostic technique but narrows the permissible scale of the conclusion
scope_limit: No evidence yet that Lovejoy read Garbe 1892 directly; genealogy of rule ≠ direct transmission
directionality: Direction requires separate evidence at each scale
